```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Liu_2026_riluzole"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Liu_2026_riluzole"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2026.1890355> (open access, PMC13661369)

Liu and colleagues built a population pharmacokinetic model of oral
riluzole from a bioequivalence study in healthy Chinese volunteers, then
used it to compare six remedial regimens for a dose of the usual 50 mg
twice-daily schedule that is taken late or missed. The model has two
compartments, first-order absorption after a lag time and linear
elimination. Body weight, normalised to 75 kg, is the only covariate and
acts on the apparent peripheral volume (Equation 1). Between-subject
variability is estimated on CL/F, Vc/F and Ka; the residual error is
combined proportional and additive.

# Population

The data come from a two-period crossover bioequivalence study of two
riluzole 50 mg tablets given fasting (Yu F et al. 2025). The 72 healthy
adults (65 men, 7 women) were 18-50 years old (median 27) and weighed
45.9-80.1 kg (median 63.3 kg; Supplementary Table S1). Each subject gave
42 plasma samples, 3,024 in all. Concentrations below the 0.700 ng/mL
limit of quantification were set to 0.35 ng/mL and kept. The model was
fitted in NONMEM 7.6.0 with FOCE-I.

# Source trace

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure | 2-compartment, first-order absorption with lag, linear elimination | Results 'PPK model development for riluzole' paragraph 1 |
| `ltlag` | log(0.157) h | Table 1 'ALAG' |
| `lka` | log(5.25) 1/h | Table 1 'Ka' |
| `lcl` | log(67) L/h | Table 1 'CL/F' |
| `lvc` | log(242) L | Table 1 'Vc/F' |
| `lq` | log(33.1) L/h | Table 1 'Q/F' |
| `lvp` | log(376) L at 75 kg | Table 1 'Vp/F'; Equation 1 |
| `e_wt_vp` | 0.993 | Table 1 'theta BW on Vp'; Equation 1 |
| Weight reference | 75 kg | Methods 'Body weight was normalized to 75 kg'; Equation 1 |
| `etalcl` | variance 0.141 | Table 1 'omega CL' (variance scale: see Assumptions) |
| `etalvc` | variance 0.218 | Table 1 'omega Vc' |
| `etalka` | variance 0.994 | Table 1 'omega Ka' |
| `propSd` | sqrt(0.127) = 0.3564 | Table 1 'Proportional' (variance) |
| `addSd` | sqrt(0.0631) = 0.2512 ng/mL | Table 1 'Additive' (variance) |
| Simulation design (remedial regimens) | 50 mg every 12 h at steady state, regimens A-F | Methods 'Optimal remedial scheme evaluation'; Figure 4 legend |

# Virtual cohort

Body weights are drawn from a normal distribution matching Supplementary
Table S1 (mean 63.9 kg, SD about 8.4 kg, truncated to the observed
45.9-80.1 kg range). Random effects are drawn with R's own random-number
generator so that the cohort is the same on every machine.

```{r cohort}
mod <- readModelDb("Liu_2026_riluzole")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
om <- ui$omega

n_sub <- 200
set.seed(20261118)
wt <- rnorm(n_sub * 3, mean = 63.9, sd = 8.4)
wt <- wt[wt >= 45.9 & wt <= 80.1][seq_len(n_sub)]
stopifnot(length(wt) == n_sub, all(!is.na(wt)))

cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  WT = wt,
  etalcl = rnorm(n_sub, 0, sqrt(om["etalcl", "etalcl"])),
  etalvc = rnorm(n_sub, 0, sqrt(om["etalvc", "etalvc"])),
  etalka = rnorm(n_sub, 0, sqrt(om["etalka", "etalka"]))
)
summary(cohort$WT)
```

# Single 50 mg dose (Figure 2)

The bioequivalence study gave single 50 mg doses and sampled to 48 h. The
simulation below includes between-subject and residual variability, as a
visual predictive check does.

```{r sim-single}
sd_times <- sort(unique(c(0, seq(0.25, 4, by = 0.25), seq(4.5, 12, by = 0.5), 13:48)))
ev_single <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = cohort$id, time = 0, amt = 50, evid = 1, cmt = "depot"),
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = cohort$id, time = sd_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central")
) |>
  left_join(cohort, by = "id") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

# The random effects are supplied per subject as data columns, so the
# model's own variances are set to zero for the solve. rxode2 then warns
# that a multi-subject solve has no omega, which is intended here; only
# that warning is muffled.
mod_fixed_re <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
solve_given_etas <- function(...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(mod_fixed_re, ..., returnType = "data.frame"),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}
sim_single <- solve_given_etas(ev_single) |>
  mutate(treatment = "50 mg single dose")

# Residual error added explicitly to the individual predictions so that the
# random-effect draws above stay under R's RNG.
prop_sd <- ui$theta[["propSd"]]
add_sd <- ui$theta[["addSd"]]
set.seed(20261119)
sim_single <- sim_single |>
  mutate(
    sd_tot = sqrt((prop_sd * Cc)^2 + add_sd^2),
    dv = Cc + rnorm(n(), 0, sd_tot)
  )

vpc <- sim_single |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(dv, 0.05), p50 = median(dv), p95 = quantile(dv, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r fig2, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 2 of Liu 2026: simulated 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles after a single 50 mg dose (lines), with the observed percentiles read from Figure 2 at the peak and at 4 h (points)."}
fig2_obs <- data.frame(
  time = c(0.75, 0.75, 0.75, 4, 4, 4),
  conc = c(445, 140, 30, 140, 56, 20),
  pct = rep(c("95th", "50th", "5th"), 2)
)
ggplot(vpc, aes(time)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_line(aes(y = p05), colour = "firebrick", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(aes(y = p95), colour = "firebrick", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(data = fig2_obs, aes(time, conc), shape = 8, colour = "black") +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Riluzole (ng/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

The observed percentiles in Figure 2 are read off the plot: median peak
about 140 ng/mL near 0.75 h, 95th percentile about 445 ng/mL, and median
about 55 ng/mL at 4 h. The typical-value prediction for a 63.3 kg subject
(the cohort median weight) is compared with them as well as the medians of
the simulated cohort:

```{r fig2-check}
ev_typ <- data.frame(
  id = 1L, time = c(0, 0.75, 4), amt = c(50, 0, 0), evid = c(1, 0, 0),
  cmt = c("depot", "central", "central"), WT = 63.3
)
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev_typ, returnType = "data.frame")
typ_peak <- typ$Cc[typ$time == 0.75]
typ_4h <- typ$Cc[typ$time == 4]
p50_peak <- max(vpc$p50)
p50_4h <- vpc$p50[vpc$time == 4]
stopifnot(length(p50_4h) == 1L, length(typ_4h) == 1L, length(typ_peak) == 1L)
data.frame(
  Quantity = c("Median peak (ng/mL)", "Concentration at 4 h (ng/mL)"),
  "Typical value" = round(c(typ_peak, typ_4h), 1),
  "Cohort median" = round(c(p50_peak, p50_4h), 1),
  "Figure 2 observed median (read off)" = c(140, 55),
  check.names = FALSE
) |>
  knitr::kable()
stopifnot(
  # Deterministic typical-value predictions against the observed medians;
  # a mis-transcribed CL/F, Vc/F, Q/F or Vp/F moves them by far more than
  # the reading error of the figure.
  abs(typ_peak / 140 - 1) < 0.25,
  abs(typ_4h / 55 - 1) < 0.15,
  # Median of the simulated cohort at the peak.
  abs(p50_peak / 140 - 1) < 0.25
)
```

The cohort median at 4 h sits somewhat below the typical value: with 200
subjects its sampling error is about 10%, and a 2,000-subject cohort
gives about 51 ng/mL.

## NCA (PKNCA)

The paper quotes a half-life of 11.4 h for riluzole in these healthy
subjects (Discussion, citing the bioequivalence study). NCA of the
individual predictions (no residual error) gives:

```{r nca}
conc <- sim_single |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose <- data.frame(id = cohort$id, time = 0, amt = 50, treatment = "50 mg single dose")

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
sim_nca <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  select(treatment, id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)

sim_nca |>
  group_by(PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = signif(median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), 3), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable()

ref_nca <- data.frame(treatment = "50 mg single dose", half.life = 11.4)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  sim_nca |> filter(PPTESTCD == "half.life"),
  ref_nca,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = attr(cmp, "footnote"))

hl_med <- median(sim_nca$PPORRES[sim_nca$PPTESTCD == "half.life"], na.rm = TRUE)
auc_med <- median(sim_nca$PPORRES[sim_nca$PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs"], na.rm = TRUE)
stopifnot(
  abs(hl_med / 11.4 - 1) < 0.2,
  # Linear model: the median AUC0-inf is Dose / (median CL/F) = 50 mg / 67 L/h.
  abs(auc_med / (50000 / 67) - 1) < 0.15
)
```

The median simulated half-life is about 12 h, against the 11.4 h quoted;
the typical-value terminal half-life of the two-compartment model is
12.7 h.

# Remedial regimens for a dose taken 1 h late (Figure 4)

The authors simulated 50 mg every 12 h to steady state, with the dose due
at 12 h taken late or missed. Their simulations kept between-subject
variability on CL/F and Vc/F and the weight effect on Vp/F, but left out
variability on Ka and the residual error (Methods 'Optimal remedial scheme
evaluation'). The reference range runs from the 5th percentile of the
steady-state trough to the 95th percentile of the steady-state
concentration 1 h after a dose. Here twenty doses at 12-h intervals bring
the cohort to steady state, and plotted time 0 is the last regular dose
before the late one.

```{r regimens}
t0 <- 240
base_doses <- seq(0, t0, by = 12)
delay <- 1
regimens <- list(
  Adherent = data.frame(time = c(12, 24, 36, 48), amt = 50),
  A = data.frame(time = c(24, 36, 48), amt = 50),
  B = data.frame(time = c(12 + delay, 24, 36, 48), amt = 50),
  C = data.frame(time = c(12 + delay, 24, 36, 48), amt = c(25, 50, 50, 50)),
  D = data.frame(time = c(12 + delay, 24, 36, 48), amt = c(50, 25, 50, 50)),
  E = data.frame(time = c(12 + delay, 36, 48), amt = c(75, 50, 50)),
  F = data.frame(time = c(24, 36, 48), amt = c(75, 50, 50))
)
obs_t <- seq(0, 60, by = 0.25)

cohort_ss <- cohort |> mutate(etalka = 0)
ev_reg <- bind_rows(lapply(names(regimens), function(r) {
  d <- bind_rows(
    data.frame(time = base_doses, amt = 50),
    regimens[[r]] |> mutate(time = time + t0)
  )
  bind_rows(
    tidyr::expand_grid(id = cohort_ss$id, d) |> mutate(evid = 1, cmt = "depot"),
    tidyr::expand_grid(id = cohort_ss$id, time = obs_t + t0) |>
      mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    mutate(regimen = r)
}))
reg_names <- names(regimens)
ev_reg <- ev_reg |>
  mutate(id = id + n_sub * (match(regimen, reg_names) - 1)) |>
  left_join(
    bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(reg_names), function(k) {
      cohort_ss |> mutate(id = id + n_sub * (k - 1))
    })),
    by = "id"
  ) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_reg <- solve_given_etas(ev_reg, keep = "regimen") |>
  mutate(ptime = time - t0)

adh <- sim_reg |> filter(regimen == "Adherent")
upper <- unname(quantile(adh$Cc[adh$ptime == 1], 0.95))
lower <- unname(quantile(adh$Cc[adh$ptime == 0], 0.05))
c(lower = lower, upper = upper)
```

```{r fig4, fig.height = 7, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4 of Liu 2026: median (line) and 5th-95th percentile band of riluzole concentration for remedial regimens A-F when the dose due at 12 h is taken 1 h late; dashed lines mark the reference range."}
band <- sim_reg |>
  filter(regimen != "Adherent") |>
  group_by(regimen, ptime) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), p50 = median(Cc), p95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(band, aes(ptime)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "pink", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(lower, upper), linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~regimen, ncol = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 60, 12)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Riluzole (ng/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

Read off Figure 4, the paper's reference range is about 4.5 to 290 ng/mL
and the steady-state median peak is about 176 ng/mL.

```{r fig4-check}
med_peak_ss <- median(adh$Cc[adh$ptime == 1])
data.frame(
  Quantity = c(
    "Upper bound: 95th pct at 1 h (ng/mL)",
    "Lower bound: 5th pct trough (ng/mL)",
    "Median at 1 h (ng/mL)"
  ),
  Simulated = round(c(upper, lower, med_peak_ss), 1),
  "Figure 4 (read off)" = c(290, 4.5, 176),
  check.names = FALSE
) |>
  knitr::kable()
stopifnot(
  # The width of the band is set by the omega scale: reading Table 1's
  # omegas as standard deviations instead of variances puts the 95th
  # percentile at about 217 ng/mL.
  abs(upper / 290 - 1) < 0.15,
  abs(med_peak_ss / 176 - 1) < 0.1,
  lower < 15
)
```

Supplementary Table S4 gives the share of the 48 h after the late dose
spent outside the reference range. The paper does not say exactly how it
was counted; its values are multiples of 1/48, which fits an hourly count
of when the 95th percentile is above the upper bound (a) or the 5th
percentile is below the lower bound (b). Counted that way:

```{r table-s4}
hourly <- band |>
  filter(ptime >= 12, ptime < 60, ptime == round(ptime)) |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(
    above_pct = round(100 * mean(p95 > upper), 2),
    below_pct = round(100 * mean(p05 < lower), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(total_pct = above_pct + below_pct)
# Supplementary Table S4, 1-h row; regimens A and F do not depend on the
# delay and are printed once for all rows.
s4 <- data.frame(
  regimen = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"),
  paper_above = c(0, 6.25, 0, 0, 2.08, 2.08),
  paper_below = c(37.5, 2.08, 16.67, 14.58, 27.08, 25)
)
hourly |>
  left_join(s4, by = "regimen") |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Regimen = regimen,
    "Above (%)" = above_pct, "Below (%)" = below_pct, "Total (%)" = total_pct,
    "Table S4 above (%)" = paper_above, "Table S4 below (%)" = paper_below
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The hourly count reproduces Supplementary Table S4 for regimens A, B, C
and F exactly and differs by one hour for D and E, which supports both the
reading of the method and the variance scale of the random effects. A
count of one hour moves with the cohort, so the table is not asserted
cell by cell; the check below asserts the paper's conclusion for this
scenario, that taking the late dose at once (regimen B) keeps the cohort
closest to the reference range, and that skipping it (regimen A) is
worst.

```{r table-s4-check}
tot <- setNames(hourly$total_pct, hourly$regimen)
stopifnot(
  all(c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F") %in% names(tot)),
  # Regimen B is best and A is worst, each by more than 4 percentage points
  # (2 h of the 48 h), twice the one-hour shifts seen against Table S4.
  tot[["B"]] + 4 < min(tot[c("C", "D", "E", "F")]),
  tot[["A"]] > max(tot[c("B", "C", "D", "E", "F")]) + 4
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Omega and sigma are variances.** Table 1 labels the random effects
  'omega CL', 'omega Vc' and 'omega Ka' and prints the residual rows
  without a scale. The base model in Supplementary Table S3 prints the
  same IIV terms as omega-squared with almost identical values (0.142,
  0.214, 0.989), and its proportional error as 35.5 %CV, which is
  sqrt(0.127). With the variance reading the model reproduces the
  reference range of Figure 4 and the hourly counts of Supplementary
  Table S4 (see above); the standard-deviation reading gives a band about
  half as wide.
* **Additive residual error.** Table 1 gives the additive term as 0.0631
  with unit ng/mL. Because the other rows of the table are NONMEM
  variances, it is read as a variance (SD 0.2512 ng/mL). Read as an SD
  instead, it would be 0.0631 ng/mL. The difference matters only near the
  0.7 ng/mL limit of quantification and does not affect any simulation in
  the paper, which left residual error out.
* **Combined error form.** The paper does not print its error equation;
  the model uses nlmixr2's default combined proportional-plus-additive
  form (variances add), which is the usual NONMEM coding.
* **Formulation.** The data pool two tablet formulations; the paper
  reports no formulation effect and the model has none.
* **Body weights of the remedial-regimen simulations.** The paper says
  the simulations included the weight effect on Vp/F but not which
  weights; the cohort here is drawn to match Supplementary Table S1.
* **Covariates screened but not retained.** Sex (on Vp/F) and age (on
  CL/F and Vc/F) were tested (Supplementary Table S2) and are recorded in
  `covariatesDataExcluded`.
* **Population.** The model was fitted to single doses in healthy
  volunteers; the authors apply it to patients with ALS at steady state
  without external validation.
* **No erratum** was found (Europe PMC and Crossref, checked 2026-11-18).
